news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway projects £764k overspend on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools
news_drafts.lead:
Dumfries and Galloway Council's education service projects overspends on two budget lines for 2026/27: £764k on Supporting Learners and £253k on primary schools. The figures are in the second-quarter revenue budget monitoring report for the Education, Skills and Community Wellbeing Committee, which meets on 10 November.

Supporting Learners has a projected out-turn of £22.705m against a revised budget of £21.941m. Additional support for learning (ASL) generic support is the largest single variance. It is projected at £1.143m over its revised budget of £13.149m. Education Psychologists, Sensory Services and Targeted Support are each projected under budget.

The primary schools line, which includes Learning Centres, has a projected out-turn of £60.288m against a revised budget of £60.035m. The paper records a £1.038m budget adjustment in 2026/27 before that revised budget was set.
news_drafts.paper_title: ESCW Q2 Revenue Budget Monitoring 202627 Appendix 1

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway: Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary allocation left a gap of about £10m
news_drafts.lead:
The money Dumfries and Galloway Council had agreed for Dumfries Academy and Loreburn Primary School does not cover the costs identified for the two schools, leaving a funding gap of around £10m. The figure is in an appendix to the council's capital investment programme, its planned spending on things that last, such as buildings, over the next few years.

The council's Education and Learning Committee agreed on 23 May 2024 that the existing allocation was not enough. That allocation is part of £73.975m in the programme. The appendix says: "Previously agreed capital allocation (part of the £73.975m) is not enough to cover the values identified, so Members also agreed to request the funding gap, circa £10m, from FTP committee."

FTP is the Finance, Procurement and Transformation Committee. The papers quoted here do not say how that committee responded to the request.

news_drafts.headline: Dumfries and Galloway council secures £50m Levelling Up grants but faces social care audit concerns
news_drafts.lead: The council has received over £50 million from the UK Government's Levelling Up Fund. Its capital projects — spending on buildings and other long-lived assets — are delivering on schedule: the Stranraer Watersports Hub is due to open in September, the Dalbeattie Rocks and Wheels facility is nearing completion, and the George building has attracted eight expressions of interest with a tender exercise in progress. The internal audit's overall opinion is Reasonable, meaning there is a generally sound system of governance, risk management and control in place. However, auditors have flagged two areas requiring ongoing monitoring: social care budgets and IT procurement, indicating these carry elevated risk requiring continuous attention.

findings.committee: Lockerbie and Lochmaben Common Good Fund Sub Committee
findings.paper_title: LLCG - Lockerbie Monitoring Report and Appendix- Draft
findings.headline: The appendix's 2026/27 financial plan includes £3,000.00 of property costs, which the report says are not in the plan.
findings.detail: The appendix shows £3,000.00 of planned property costs, with nothing spent to date and the same amount forecast. The report's section on expenditure states that no property costs are currently included within the 2026/27 Financial Plan.
findings.matters: A planned property cost that one document includes and another excludes changes the expected spend and the forecast balance, so a reader needs to know which is correct.
findings.figures: £3,000.00 property costs in the financial plan, £0.00 actual spend to date, £3,000.00 forecast outturn

findings.committee: Lockerbie and Lochmaben Common Good Fund Sub Committee
findings.paper_title: LLCG - Lockerbie Monitoring Report and Appendix- Draft
findings.headline: The appendix's monitoring statement shows a forecast closing cash balance of £39,618.56 and estimated free income of -£1,377.00, while the report gives £30,965.33 and £2,937.00.
findings.detail: The appendix opens the year with a cash balance of £40,995.56, against £28,028.33 in the report. Its forecast income of £1,729.00 and expenditure of £3,106.00 also differ from the report's £3,445.00 and £508.00, yet the report recommends noting that income and expenditure are in line with the approved plan.
findings.matters: A committee paper whose summary and monitoring statement give different balances and free income figures is one a finance director would want reconciled before relying on the forecast.
findings.figures: Report: £28,028.33 opening, £30,965.33 closing, £2,937.00 free income. Appendix: £40,995.56 opening, £39,618.56 closing, -£1,377.00 estimated free income, £1,729.00 plan income, £3,106.00 plan expenditure

findings.committee: Lockerbie and Lochmaben Common Good Fund Sub Committee
findings.paper_title: LLCG - Lockerbie Monitoring Report and Appendix- Draft
findings.headline: The report forecasts a 2026/27 closing cash balance of £30,965.33, an increase of £2,937.00 on the opening balance of £28,028.33.
findings.detail: The report says the forecast net income for the year is £2,937.00, from forecast income of £3,445.00 less forecast expenditure of £508.00. It describes the forecast free income as available for future grant support, asset maintenance or community projects.
findings.matters: A forecast rise in a small reserve, with its uses named, shows how a council plans to use accumulated balances, and that depends on the appendix figures being right.
findings.figures: £30,965.33 forecast closing cash balance at 31 March 2027; £28,028.33 opening cash balance; £2,937.00 forecast increase; £3,445.00 forecast income; £508.00 forecast expenditure
findings.quote: The forecast closing cash balance at 31 March 2027 is therefore £30,965.33, representing a positive movement of £2,937.00 over the financial year.

findings.committee: Lockerbie and Lochmaben Common Good Fund Sub Committee
findings.paper_title: LLCG - Lockerbie Monitoring Report and Appendix- Draft
findings.headline: Lockerbie Golf Club's 2026/27 rent of £1,000.00 has been received in full, which the report describes as an improvement on previous years.
findings.detail: The report states that the full annual rent from Lockerbie Golf Club has already been received for 2026/27. It adds that this is an improvement on previous years and gives additional assurance on future income streams.
findings.matters: Full receipt of an annual rent before year end is a concrete income outcome that a finance director can compare with the same asset's collection in other years or at other councils.
findings.figures: £1,000.00 rent received from Lockerbie Golf Club; £1,000.00 is the full annual rent in the approved financial plan
findings.quote: Rental income of £1,000.00 has already been received from Lockerbie Golf Club

findings.committee: Lockerbie and Lochmaben Common Good Fund Sub Committee
findings.paper_title: LLCG - Lochmaben Monitoring Report and Appendix - Draft
findings.headline: £3,000.00 is provided within the 2026/27 financial plan for property-related costs, and no expenditure had been incurred at the time of reporting.
findings.detail: The paper says the £3,000.00 provision is for property costs 'which may arise during the year', so the spend is not yet committed. The paper also notes a £106.00 administrative charge from Dumfries and Galloway Council, which is forecast and not yet paid.
findings.matters: The reserve drawdown depends on a provision whose timing and amount are still unknown, so the forecast deficit could move in either direction.
findings.figures: Property costs provision £3,000.00; expenditure to date £0.00; forecast administrative charge £106.00.
findings.quote: No expenditure has been incurred at the time of reporting.
